## Overview

LRP84 is the phoneme-blending companion to [`lrp-rli-dose-077`](../lrp-rli-dose-077/) (word reading), completing the dose-response family's coverage of the two largest available-case modified ITT estimates (`L` and `B`). The estimand, causal structure and caveats are identical to LRP77; only the outcome changes.

**Estimand.** Among children who were **receiving** the intervention, how blending _conditional change_ relates to how many sessions they attended, with partial pooling across the three periods and a test of whether the attendance–gain slope **varies by period**. The outcome is the Beta-Binomial post-count of $B$ conditional on its own baseline logit ($N = 10$) — conditional change, not a raw change score. All three phase transitions are stacked with reference-coded phase intercepts:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\eta = {} & \alpha + \alpha_{\text{phase}[p]}
     + \theta_{\text{treated}}\,\mathbb{1}[\text{on intervention}]
     + \beta_{\text{arm,late}}\,G\,\mathbb{1}[p \ge 2] \\
    & + \gamma_{\text{own}}\,\text{logit}(B_{\text{pre}})
     + \gamma_A\,z(\text{age})
     + u_{\text{child}} \\
    & + \beta_{\text{between}}\,\bar{d}_{\text{child}}
     + \beta_{\text{dose}[p]}\,(d - \bar{d}_{\text{child}})
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\beta_{\text{dose}[p]} = \mu_{\text{dose}} + \sigma_{\text{dose}}\,z_p$ (partial-pooled period slopes) and $\alpha_{\text{phase}[1]} = 0$ (period 1 is the reference). $d$ is sessions attended, centred and standardised over the on-intervention rows only.

## Separating "was taught" from "attended more"

In period 1 every immediate-arm child attended 45–91 sessions and every waiting-control child attended none, so assigned arm and session count correlate at **0.970**. A single dose coefficient spanning both groups would therefore report the randomised treatment contrast divided by the mean session count, not an attendance effect. Sessions enter centred and standardised over the **on-intervention rows only** (zero elsewhere), the indicator $\theta_{\text{treated}}$ carries the extensive margin, and the exposure is split Mundlak-style into each child's study-average attendance ($\beta_{\text{between}}$) and their deviation from it ($\beta_{\text{dose}[p]}$). See the [LRP77 report](../lrp-rli-dose-077/) for the full treatment.

## Adjustment set (revised DAG)

The focal edge is $\text{sessions} \to \text{outcome}$. The DAG gives **no clean back-door set**: `IS` has parents $A \to IS$, $GA \to IS$ and $IG \to IS$, and all three also point into the outcomes. Age and assigned group are measured and adjusted; **latent general ability $GA$ is not**, and no measured baseline closes it — Frank's 2012 caveat (the least-able children attended least) is exactly this path. $G$ (arm, coded $G = 2-\text{group}$, positive = benefit) enters from period 2 onward only, where both arms are on the intervention and arm reads as intervention _order_; in period 1 it would be exactly collinear with the on-intervention indicator. $B_{\text{pre}}$ is the autoregression / RTM control (parameterisation, not back-door blocking). **Cumulative dose** (`attend_cumul`) is a descendant of the `IS` collider, is **not** conditioned on (it reopens the latent-ability back door, #269) and is not fitted here. The waiting controls' period-1 zero-session rows identify the on-intervention contrast; they contribute nothing to the dose terms.

_Adjusted association, not "more sessions cause more gain"._ Attendance is **not** randomised (only assignment is), so every dose slope here is an adjusted association, and the unblocked $GA \to IS$ path is a live confounder; the subject random intercept absorbs only _stable_ child differences, which is why the exposure is additionally split into between-child and within-child components. The one randomised quantity in this fit is the period-1 on-intervention contrast $\theta_{\text{treated}}$. The corresponding randomised-arm result is the available-case modified ITT estimate in `lrp-rli-itt-008`, with its stated missing-data qualification.
